drivingQuestion: From where in Scripture is it derived that a man may dedicate only part of what he owns, and why does the verse also say בהמה?
outcomeNote: The verse's partitive phrases yield the mishna's rule, each is shown to be necessary, and בהמה is assigned its own derivation.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״מִכׇּל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ״ — וְלֹא כׇּל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ, ״מֵאָדָם״ — וְלֹא כׇּל אָדָם, ״מִבְּהֵמָה״ — וְלֹא כׇּל בְּהֵמָה, ״מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה״ — וְלֹא כׇּל שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The Gemara asks: «From where are these matters,» stated in the mishna, derived? The Gemara explains that this is «as the Sages taught» in a baraita, with regard to the verse: “Notwithstanding, no dedicated thing that a man may dedicate to the Lord of all that he has, whether of man or animal, or of his ancestral field” (Leviticus 27:28). The verse indicates that one may dedicate «“of all that he has” but not all that he has;» likewise «“of man” but not every man,» i.e., not every slave of his; “of man «or animal” but not every animal» of his; and finally one may dedicate «“of» his «ancestral field” but not all of» his «ancestral field.»

segments.he: יָכוֹל לֹא יַחְרִים, וְאִם הֶחְרִים יְהוּ מוּחְרָמִין? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אַךְ״, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר. אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה: מָה אִם לַגָּבוֹהַּ אֵין אָדָם רַשַּׁאי לְהַחְרִים כׇּל נְכָסָיו, עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה שֶׁיְּהֵא אָדָם חָס עַל נְכָסָיו!
segments.en: It «might» have been thought that «one may not dedicate» all his properties ab initio, «but if he did dedicate» all of them, «they should be dedicated.» Therefore «the verse states: “Notwithstanding,”» to teach that they are not dedicated. This is «the statement of Rabbi Eliezer. Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya said: If for the Most High a person may not dedicate all his property,» it is «all the more so» the case «that a person should spare his property» and not give it all to others.

segments.he: וּצְרִיכָא, דְּאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״מִכׇּל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ״, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: כֹּל דְּאִית לֵיהּ לָא לַחְרֵים, אֲבָל מִין אֶחָד לַיחְרְמֵיהּ כּוּלֵּיהּ, כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״מֵאָדָם״ — וְלֹא כׇּל אָדָם.
segments.en: The Gemara notes: «And» it is «necessary» to derive this halakha with regard to all the categories in the verse. «As, if the Merciful One had written» only: «“Of all that he has,” I would say» that «one may not dedicate all that he has, but let him dedicate all of one type» of property. Therefore, «the Merciful One writes “of man,”» to teach that he may «not» dedicate «every man.»

segments.he: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״מֵאָדָם״, דְּלָא סַגִּיא לֵיהּ בְּלָא עֲבוֹדָה, אֲבָל שָׂדֶה — סַגִּיא לֵיהּ בְּדִיסְתּוּרָן. וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן הָנֵי תַּרְתֵּי, מִשּׁוּם דְּהָכָא חִיּוּתָא וְהָכָא חִיּוּתָא, אֲבָל מְטַלְטְלִין — לַיחְרְמִינְהוּ כּוּלְּהוּ, צְרִיכִי.
segments.en: «And if the Merciful One had written» only: «“of man,”» one might say that he may not dedicate all of his slaves, «as it is not possible for him» to be «without» a slave to perform his «work; but» with regard to «a field, it is possible for him» to maintain a livelihood «by sharecropping [distoran]. And if» the Torah «had taught» this halakha with regard to only «these two» types, i.e., ancestral fields and slaves, one might say these may not be dedicated in their entirety «because here» there is «livelihood and here» there is also «livelihood. But» in the case of «movable property,» on which maintaining a livelihood does not depend, «let him dedicate all of them.» Therefore, all of these derivations «are necessary.»

segments.he: ״בְּהֵמָה״ לְמָה לִי? לְכִדְתַנְיָא: יָכוֹל יַחְרִים אָדָם בְּנוֹ וּבִתּוֹ, עַבְדּוֹ וְשִׁפְחָתוֹ הָעִבְרִיִּים, וּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָתוֹ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״בְּהֵמָה״, מָה בְּהֵמָה יֵשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְמוֹכְרָהּ, אַף כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְמוֹכְרָהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara further asks: «Why do I» need for the verse to state “or «animal”?» The Gemara explains it is necessary «for that which is taught» in a baraita: One «might» have thought «a person can dedicate his son or his daughter, his Hebrew slave or maidservant, or his purchased field.» Therefore, «the verse states “animal”» to teach that «just as an animal» is an item «that he has permission to sell, so too,» one can dedicate «any» item «that he has permission to sell.» He cannot dedicate an item that he does not have the ability to sell.

segments.he: וַהֲלֹא בִּתּוֹ קְטַנָּה יֵשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְמוֹכְרָהּ, יָכוֹל יַחְרִימֶנָּה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״בְּהֵמָה״, מָה בְּהֵמָה יֵשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְמוֹכְרָהּ לְעוֹלָם, אַף כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְמוֹכְרָהּ לְעוֹלָם.
segments.en: The baraita continues: «But» in the case of «his minor daughter, he has permission to sell her» as a Hebrew maidservant. If so, one «might» have thought «he may dedicate her.» Therefore, «the verse states “animal,”» indicating that «just as an animal» is an item «that he always has permission to sell, so too,» one can dedicate «any» item «that he always has permission to sell,» whereas one may not sell his daughter once she reaches majority. A field as well can be sold only until the Jubilee Year.

moves.about: the scriptural source for the mishna's rule that one may not dedicate all of any category of his property

moves.summary: brings the baraita that supplies the derivation
moves.about: brings the baraita that derives the mishna's rule from the wording of the dedication verse

moves.cueHe: ״מכל אשר לו״ — ולא כל אשר לו
moves.summary: each partitive phrase of the verse excludes dedicating a whole category
moves.about: quotes the four limiting phrases of the dedication verse as the material of the derivation

moves.cueHe: יכול לא יחרים, ואם החרים יהו מוחרמין?
moves.summary: raises the possibility that the prohibition is only ab initio
moves.about: the baraita names Rabbi Eliezer as the author of the derivation from אך

moves.summary: the word אך blocks the dedication even after the fact
moves.about: the word אך is read as a restriction, so that a dedication of everything does not take effect even after the fact

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: מה אם לגבוה אין אדם רשאי
moves.summary: draws the a fortiori that a person should spare his own property
moves.about: if one may not dedicate all his property even to the Most High, all the more should a person spare his property from being given to men

moves.cueHe: וצריכא, דאי כתב רחמנא ״מכל אשר לו״
moves.summary: shows why the phrase of man is needed alongside of all that he has
moves.about: quotes the verse's phrases again in order to show that each of them is needed

moves.summary: completes the necessity argument through field and movable property
moves.about: each of the verse's limiting phrases is necessary, since none could be derived from the others

moves.summary: asks what the word animal adds to the derivation
moves.about: why the verse needed to write בהמה at all, once the other limitations are in place

moves.summary: brings a baraita limiting dedication to what a man may sell
moves.about: brings a second baraita which uses בהמה to limit dedication to what a man is permitted to sell

moves.cueHe: והלא בתו קטנה יש לו רשות למוכרה
moves.summary: a minor daughter may be sold, so the derivation would admit her
moves.about: a minor daughter can be sold, so the derivation as first stated would let a man dedicate her

moves.cueHe: תלמוד לומר: ״בהמה״, מה בהמה יש לו רשות למוכרה לעולם
moves.summary: refines the derivation to what may be sold at any time, excluding a daughter past minority
moves.about: בהמה is refined to what he may sell always, excluding a daughter who may be sold only in her minority
